en.headline: Red Cross map shows northern districts face highest disaster risk
en.dek: A new Hong Kong Red Cross study finds 14.7 per cent of the territory is at extreme risk from typhoons, extreme heat or fires, with Yuen Long and North District the most exposed.
body: The Hong Kong Red Cross has released a Disaster Risk and Coping Capacity Map showing that nearly 15 per cent of Hong Kong faces extreme disaster risk, with the highest concentrations in Yuen Long and the North District.

The study, which assessed exposure, vulnerability and response capacity against typhoons, extreme heat and fires, found that more than half the territory is exposed to two or more high or extreme risks. Remote areas such as Pat Heung have typhoon shelters more than four times farther than the citywide average, while fire-drill participation remains low in several high-risk urban districts.

The Red Cross urged the government to incorporate disaster-risk considerations into Northern Metropolis planning, convert community facilities into emergency shelters, and adopt more localised preparedness measures rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.

zh.headline: 紅十字會災害風險地圖 元朗北區風險最高
zh.dek: 香港紅十字會研究顯示全港近15%地區屬極端災害風險，元朗及北區最集中，超過一半地區同時面對兩種或以上高風險。
body: 香港紅十字會公布《香港災害風險及應對能力地圖》，指出全港約14.7%地區屬極端災害風險，最高風險集中在元朗及北區。
研究以颱風、極端高溫及火災為評估對象，發現超過一半地區同時面對兩種或以上高或極端風險。八鄉等偏遠地區最近的颱風避難所距離較全港平均遠逾四倍，而部分高風險市區的防火演習參與率亦偏低。
紅十字會建議政府在北部都會區規劃中納入災害風險考慮，將社區設施改作緊急庇護所，並採取更針對地區需要的防災措施。
